title: Inside the mknoon app — the first layer
subtitle: The big picture drew the app as one box. This opens that box. Every number on this page is counted from the codebase, not typed by hand.

boundary.label: Inside the mknoon app — one phone

_claim_order: A file that matches several components goes to the first one listed here.

components.name: You
blurb: Tapping the screen.
components.desc: Sets up an account with a 12-word phrase, adds people by scanning a code, then chats one to one or in groups.

components.name: The screens
blurb: Every screen and button: chats, groups, the feed,
your circle of contacts, the QR code, settings.
Also holds the rules — what counts as unread,
when to retry a send, what a banner should say.
components.desc: Draws every screen and decides what happens when you tap. Holds the everyday rules too: what counts as unread, when to retry a message that failed, what a banner should say.

components.name: The engine
components.type: the heavy lifting, built into the app
blurb: Makes your keys from the 12 words. Locks a message
so only your friend can open it, and unlocks theirs.
Keeps the line to other phones open, finds them
again when the network changes, and hands
finished messages up to the screens.
components.desc: All the maths and all the networking. Turns your 12 words into keys, locks a message so only your friend can open it, unlocks the ones that arrive, and keeps the line to other phones open as you move between Wi-Fi and mobile data.

components.name: The locked notebook
blurb: Every chat, contact, group, photo,
voice note and reaction. Locked, so
nobody can read it by pulling the
file off the phone.
components.desc: Where everything is kept: chats, contacts, groups, photos, voice notes, reactions. The whole file is locked, so pulling it off the phone gets you nothing readable.

components.name: The safe
blurb: The few real secrets: your 12
words, your private keys, and
the key that opens the locked
notebook. The phone guards it
and opens it only for you.
components.desc: Holds only the few real secrets — your 12 words, your private keys, and the key that opens the locked notebook. The phone guards it and hands it over only when you have unlocked the device.

components.name: The alert helper
blurb: Wakes up when an alert arrives,
even when the app is closed.
Fetches the message that was
waiting and rewrites the banner,
so you see the real text instead
of just "New message".
components.desc: Runs on its own when an alert arrives, even if the app is fully closed. Fetches the message that was waiting and rewrites the banner, so you see the real text rather than “New message”. There is one on iPhone and one on Android.

components.name: The outside world
blurb: Your friend's phone, the helper server and the alert services.
They are all drawn in the big picture.
components.desc: Your friend's phone, the helper server and the alert services. Drawn in the big picture, not here.

story.title: What happens when a message arrives
steps: Your friend's phone sends it. If your app is open, it lands straight away — the engine takes it and passes it to the screens.
If your phone was off or the app was closed, the helper server keeps it and asks the alert service to tap your phone.
The alert helper wakes up, fetches the waiting message, and puts the real text into the banner you see.
When you open the app, the screens ask the engine for anything still outstanding.
The engine takes the keys out of the safe and unlocks the message.
The screens write it into the locked notebook and show it in the chat.

notes.title: Worth knowing
items: Only the engine talks to the outside.
The screens never touch the network on their own. They ask the engine, and the engine answers.
The safe is small on purpose.
It holds a handful of secrets, not your data. Everything else goes in the locked notebook, and the key to that notebook lives in the safe.
The alert helper is a different program.
It has its own small copy of the engine, because the app may not be running at all when an alert lands.
The busiest wire has the thinnest safety net.
Everything the app does passes between the screens and the engine, yet that is the one connection where no test holds both ends at once, unless it runs on a real phone.
There is also a small share-sheet helper on iPhone, for sending a photo from another app into mknoon. It is a side door, left out to keep the drawing simple.
